name: PulsePoint ThermoSet Thermal Regulation Implant
description:
The ThermoSet is a spinal implant seated at the cervical-thoracic junction that intercepts and augments the body's existing thermoregulatory signaling through the hypothalamus-spinal axis. It does not generate heat or cooling directly; instead, it modulates peripheral vasodilation and vasoconstriction responses, sweat gland activation thresholds, and the rate of metabolic heat generation in brown adipose tissue. The net effect is a significant expansion of the user's thermal comfort zone — the range of ambient temperatures that feel neutral rather than uncomfortable. A standard unaugmented human becomes noticeably uncomfortable around 16°C or above 30°C; ThermoSet users report effective comfort across roughly 8°C to 38°C ambient. The implant draws on a spinal-flex microgenerator and requires no external power. A paired subdermal thermistor array across the upper back provides real-time ambient data to the control node.

In a city like GLMZ, where winters in the Great Lakes corridor are brutal and the Gray Zone districts have inconsistent climate infrastructure, the ThermoSet is less a luxury than a quality-of-life necessity for many residents. Outdoor workers — couriers, construction crews, agricultural transit staff — commonly have it installed as a job prerequisite or strong professional recommendation. Tier 1 residents living in under-heated buildings find it transformative: the implant doesn't make a cold room warm, but it makes a cold room survivable and even comfortable. Summer heat waves, increasingly severe through the 2190s, have driven installation rates sharply upward. The feeling of walking outside into a Meridian August and simply not minding is, for many users, the single most impactful quality-of-life change any implant has ever given them.
installation_requirements: Outpatient clinic with licensed installer; 45-minute procedure, mild sedation, no overnight stay required; installation by spinal-adjacent implant technician (not a full surgeon)
maintenance: Annual calibration recommended to adjust seasonal comfort range profiles; spinal-flex generator is self-sustaining; firmware updates downloadable at any PulsePoint kiosk

side_effects: First two weeks may include unpredictable sweating responses while the system calibrates baseline
Some users report a brief 'flush' sensation when the implant actively compensates for rapid temperature changes
Rare: mild stiffness at C7-T1 installation site, resolves within three months
Users occasionally report reduced ability to notice dangerous cold or heat without conscious attention — the body no longer screams warnings it used to
cultural_context: The ThermoSet occupies a curious middle ground in GLMZ's social landscape. In Tier 1 and Tier 2 communities it is seen as intensely practical — a working person's implant, something you get so you can do your job and live your life without the weather becoming an obstacle. In Tier 3 and above, it's common but unremarkable, the way decent insulation in a home is unremarkable. Among Spire residents, custom high-end equivalents exist under boutique brand names, but the function is identical. There is no stigma attached to it, and it is one of the few implants that crosses all social tiers without class signaling in either direction. Outdoor laborers sometimes get the brand logo tattooed near the installation site as a mark of professional identity — 'I work outside and I don't blink.'
known_users: the Gray Zone residents in under-heated housing
story_hooks: A dockworker found dead in a the Gray Zone alley in January shows no signs of hypothermia despite sub-zero temperatures and inadequate clothing — their ThermoSet was functioning perfectly, masking what should have been distress signals until far too late

A recall notice has been quietly issued for a specific ThermoSet firmware batch that occasionally inverts its response — users in a heatwave have been feeling cold and dressing warmly, accelerating heat stroke

Someone is selling black-market ThermoSet override codes that push the implant's upper limit well beyond its designed ceiling — useful for people who need to work in industrial heat environments without protective gear, but the long-term neurological cost is unknown
